pages.text: Shops lined the market alley. Mom gave them coins and waved.
They wanted to buy salt by themselves. Mom said, "Salt smells like the sea."
Lolo went straight to a white sack. Riri examined the shops one by one. "Anything white is salt." "We must find the right thing."
Lolo grabbed the first white sack. "Found it!"
The shopkeeper smiled. "Dear, that is sugar."
Riri peered at every white thing. This was flour, and that was rice.
White sacks stretched to the end of the alley. Riri's hands were covered in white powder.
Riri sniffed. One sack smelled like the sea.
They stood side by side at that sack and sniffed. Salt!
Mom took the salt. Lolo was holding a bag of sugar too. Mom shook the bag and said, "Doughnuts for dinner tonight, then."
